/about/.title: The idea behind DotiDoit
/about/.description: Make room in everyday life for what matters to you, one action at a time.
/about/.markdown:
# Small actions for the things that matter
A walk, a workout, a kind word to your parents. DotiDoit gives your intentions a place in everyday life: choose what to do, do it, and look back at your record.
## A reason in your own words
Your reason need not be ambitious. Add a personal goal and mission description that will still mean something when you read them later.
## Goals that fit your life
Start with a Doti mission or create your own. Choose the threshold, time period and records that make sense for you. A routine prepares the sequence of activities, rests and repeats.
## Recording should stay manageable
Measure an activity now, enter a completed activity, or connect ongoing measurement for supported metrics. Keep numbers alongside a photo or a note. You can create a feed post without linking a mission.
## Room to start again
Some days you reach the goal; other days you don't. Review your records, adjust your goal and decide on your next step.
[Start your first mission](/guides/start-a-mission/)

/missions/.title: Missions and success criteria
/missions/.description: Set a goal, choose its success criteria and record activities in a way that suits you.
/missions/.markdown:
# A mission for something you want to do
A mission combines an intention with a way to check its result. Choose a ready-made Doti mission or create one of your own. “Official” means supplied by Doti, not certified by a public or medical institution.
## Choose your success criteria
In mission creation or editing, set the period, measurement, minimum or maximum, value and unit. Examples include at least 10,000 steps in a day or 30 minutes of exercise accumulated over a day. Set the target number of successes and the deadline too.
Add your personal goal below the mission name and explain your reason in the description.
## Ways to record
Open **Record mission** to enter the date and results directly, including earlier dates and separate entries on the same day. To measure now, choose **Measure and record** on that screen. Time is optional unless the success criterion requires it; enter it yourself or use the current-time button.
**Ongoing measurement:** supported when the success metric is total steps or last phone-use end. Consent, relevant permissions and a compatible source are required. Adding an arbitrary metric does not enable automatic recording.
## Required metrics and changes
Measurement and manual entry use one shared list of metrics. The success-criterion metric and activity time stay enabled; other reference metrics are optional. Changing a criterion reassesses existing and in-progress records without changing their original measurements, photos or notes.
## Several sessions in one day
Review each session in the dated history. Its list summarizes up to three lines; measurement details show the full time-by-time entries. A day's achievement follows the mission's configured criteria.

## Detailed goals and progress

In mission creation and editing, review the name, description, deadline, target success count and success criteria. Detailed goals can be added or edited separately. Achieved dates use orange bars and Success! labels. The history chart and tree icons open measured values and routine details.

[Your first mission](/guides/start-a-mission/) · [Walking records](/guides/walking-records/)

## Read automatic results
Automatic records show the goal result to the right of measured values. Distinguish confirmed success, a currently met goal while aggregation continues, and missing evidence needing review. A zero measurement and unavailable evidence can share a not-achieved label, but their source states and detailed explanations remain distinct. Automatic-record cards can include the goal result too.

/routines/.title: Plan your activity sequence
/routines/.description: Arrange activities, timing, rests and repeats into a routine you can follow.
/routines/.markdown:
# Several activities, one sequence
A mission says what you want to achieve; a routine prepares the order in which to act.
## Start with a Doti routine
Browse Doti routines for strength, running, breathing and more. Review the total time and activity structure, including warm-up and recovery, before choosing.
## Adjust timing and repeats
Create or edit a routine's image, name, activities and timing. Group activities and repeat the group. You can copy an activity to add another with the same settings, then edit it.
## Follow it with a mission
Select the routine in mission details, open Record mission, then choose Measure and record. Planned duration and actual performance are separate; the mission criterion determines success.
While measuring, pause before selecting, replacing, removing or editing a routine. Earlier completed repetitions and partial activity time remain in the record. A replacement routine prepares its first activity and waits for Resume; without a routine, elapsed time and selected sensors continue after Resume. Reopen a temporarily saved session before making changes.
## Share the structure
Routine sharing produces images showing the name, duration, activities and repeats. Long routines may use multiple images. Receiving an image does not automatically install a routine in another person's app.

## Routine hierarchy and results

History and record cards retain parent and child activities. Select parent names and child results independently on a card. Repeated activities combine only within the same parent; rests in different groups are not added together.

[Use an exercise routine](/guides/exercise-routine/)

/records/.title: History, photos and your feed
/records/.description: Create a video post: History, photos and your feed
/records/.markdown:
# Records and feeds

## History and goal results
History groups performances by date and time. Automatic records show steps, duration or other measured values beside the goal result. Confirmed success, a goal currently met while aggregation continues, and evidence needing review are distinct states. The chart icon opens measurements; the tree icon opens routine details with their hierarchy.

## From media to a feed
Attach a photo, video or record card, review the mission and performance date/time, write a note, then choose records. At least one attachment is required. Cards are not created automatically. You can also make a photo/video and note feed without a mission.
Saving a direct entry and choosing to write a feed uses that one saved performance and its date. A whole-day feed brings together that day's records by field. The date, time and primary result at the top remain independent of the record checkboxes. Duration seconds are displayed without decimals; source precision is preserved.

## Choose records on the page
A feed containing only direct entries includes their values in the body without exclusion checkboxes here; measurements and routines are shown as absent. A mixed day uses Measured values (includes manual entries).
Measurement and routine checklists appear directly on the feed page. A group checkbox selects or clears its own indented fields. Items excluded from the feed start unchecked in the card editor too. Rechecking one in the card editor adds it only to the card and leaves the feed-body exclusion unchanged.

## Basic data, measured values and routine records
The card editor's records tab has three peer groups: Basic data, Measured values and Routine records. Each group checkbox affects only its own fields and shows partial selection. Select all and Deselect all apply across groups.
Basic data contains Mission name, Date, Performance time of day and Duration. Depending on the record, Mission result replaces Duration; automatic-record cards can include their goal result too. Unavailable time or result fields cannot be selected. Time comes from direct entries or measurement; several times are summarized by the first time and an indication of more. Header time and measurement time are selected separately.
Select parent routine names and child activities independently. Hiding a parent leaves child selections intact. Repetitions merge only within the same parent, so rests in different groups stay separate. Names align left and recorded values align right.

## Design your card
Doti images for an official mission bring its matching report background into view first. New Doti backgrounds use 0% dimming without changing original photos or mission covers. Choose Report, Big numbers, Journal or Minimal, with a digital-clock default font and formatting for all text, individual items, labels, values or units.
Date, time and duration or result use their actual text widths with compact gaps; hidden fields leave no empty slot. The card displays measurement and routine headings and hierarchy. Dense records use two columns and long values wrap rather than shrinking that value alone. Automatic decorations adapt to one or two columns.

## View and share
Collapsed feeds show performance date/time and a note summary. More reveals indented data beneath measurement and routine headings; collapse hides the details again. The same date is not repeated. Photos support zoom in their viewer. Videos play automatically, muted and looping, in place.
Saving a feed does not publish it to others. Check the destination and included data before sharing. Feed/card edits do not change source performances or statistics. Shared video is a locally generated MP4 of the selected segment and visible records. ZIP backups include the entire original video, including trimmed-out portions.

[Video feeds](/guides/video-feed/) · [Missions](/missions/)

/faq/.title: Frequently asked questions
/faq/.description: Answers about missions, permissions, ongoing measurement, languages and sharing.
/faq/.markdown:
# Frequently asked questions
## Is this only for exercise?
No. Walking, exercise and everyday intentions can all become missions. Measure without a mission, or keep a feed post with photos and notes alone.
## Is everything recorded automatically?
No. Ongoing measurement supports total steps and last phone-use end as success metrics. Other activities can be measured or entered manually. Permission and device support affect availability.
## What does last phone-use end mean?
It is a time derived from phone-use information, not a measurement of sleep or use of other devices.
## Why is GPS not ready?
Check location permission and the phone's location setting. The activity screen offers an action when a required permission is missing. Permission alone does not guarantee a GPS fix; reception can be poor indoors.
## Does finishing a routine guarantee success?
No. The mission's criteria and the saved results determine success. A routine describes the activity sequence.
## Do record cards appear automatically?
No. Choose an image and the records to include when making a post, including from ongoing measurements. Existing saved cards remain editable.
## Which languages can I choose?
Settings → Language offers Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Spanish and Vietnamese. The choice persists after restart. Follow device language uses a supported phone preference, or English if none is supported. Your own titles and notes are not automatically translated.
## Are my records shared automatically?
No. Saving and external sharing are separate. Select what to share and the receiving app and person. Routine images are readable content; receiving one does not automatically register a routine.
[Getting started](/download/) · [First mission](/guides/start-a-mission/)
## Can I post videos?
Supported versions import album videos with trimming, layout and record overlays. Playback starts muted; the speaker controls preview sound. Exported MP4 audio is set separately in video tools. ZIP backups contain the complete original, even trimmed-out parts.
## What about older routine links?
Importing server-based routine links is no longer supported. Official missions and Doti images are built into the app and added through updates. Receiving a routine image does not register a routine.

[Create a video post](/guides/video-feed/)

## Can I record an activity I already finished?
Open **Record mission**, choose the date and enter the values. Add separate entries for sessions on the same date. Time can stay empty unless the criterion requires it. For a new measurement, choose **Measure and record** on the same screen.

## Can I exclude manually entered values from a post?

A manual-only post includes the entered values in its caption without exclusion checkboxes on this screen. Measured values and routines show None. For days with both manual and measured records, choose values in Measured values (includes manual entries). Photo and video overlay selections are separate. A post needs at least one photo, video or manually created record card.

/download/.title: Get started with DotiDoit
/download/.description: Find DotiDoit on Google Play and choose your first goal, recording method and language.
/download/.markdown:
# Get started with DotiDoit
Search Google Play for DotiDoit. Check device compatibility and the features offered by the installed version. Screens and availability may differ by app version and device.
## Start with one mission
Choose a familiar goal. Review its success criteria, then decide whether to measure now or enter an activity already completed. For ongoing measurement, read the consent notice and grant the necessary permissions, then check that records arrive.
## Choose your language
Settings → Language offers Korean, English, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Spanish and Vietnamese. You can also follow device language. The choice is saved; your own mission names and notes stay unchanged.
## Add more when you need it
Link a routine when you want a planned sequence. Add photos, selected records and notes when you want a feed post. You do not need to configure everything on day one.
[First mission](/guides/start-a-mission/) · [FAQ](/faq/)

/guides/start-a-mission/.title: Your first mission
/guides/start-a-mission/.description: Choose a goal, review its criteria and save your first activity.
/guides/start-a-mission/.markdown:
# Start your first mission
Choose one familiar thing you can try today.
## Pick a mission
Use + on Missions to choose a Doti mission or create your own. You can also start with a mission already in your list.
## Check the goal and measurements
Review the success period, metric, threshold, target count and deadline. Add a personal goal or a reason. Metrics used by the criterion remain enabled in measurement settings.
## Record today's activity
Open **Record mission** to enter a date and values, including yesterday. Add another entry for a separate session on the same date. Time can stay empty unless the criterion requires it, or you can fill the current time. To start measuring, tap **Measure and record** on the same screen. Daily steps require consent and permissions; route recording also needs location access.
## Look back at the result
Check progress and the dated history. Select a session or a date to create a feed post, then choose the image and record fields to include. Saving the result is sufficient; posting is optional.
[Missions](/missions/) · [Records and feed](/records/)

/guides/walking-records/.title: Daily steps and a single walk
/guides/walking-records/.description: Understand daily accumulation, permissions and the scope of a walking session.
/guides/walking-records/.markdown:
# Daily steps and a single walk
Your commute, lunch walk and steps at home can contribute to a daily total. A measured walk covers one particular session.
## Set a daily goal
Choose total steps as the criterion and enable ongoing measurement. Review consent, step access and activity permissions as prompted, then check the recording status.
## Starting in the afternoon
When the data source contains that day's steps and access is allowed, steps since 00:00 count for display and success, even before the mission's start time. Missing source data cannot be invented.
## Measure a particular walk
Start measurement and choose the needed metrics. A route needs location settings and permission. You can measure without creating a mission.
## Avoid counting the same steps twice
A workout's steps may already be in the daily total; do not add the two together. Check each history entry's date and scope.
## If data is delayed
Check recording status, permissions and the data source. Changing a goal and connecting a data source are separate actions. Values may arrive later.
[FAQ](/faq/) · [Mission settings](/missions/)

/guides/exercise-routine/.title: Use a routine with an exercise mission
/guides/exercise-routine/.description: Prepare the goal and sequence, review permissions and save the actual result.
/guides/exercise-routine/.markdown:
# Prepare your goal and activity sequence
A routine helps organize how you exercise; a mission holds the goal you want to check.
## Check the mission goal
Review its time threshold, success period and deadline. Different criteria can produce different results from the same workout.
## Review the whole routine
Check activities, repeats, warm-up, rests and recovery. A routine with “30 minutes” in its name may take longer when preparation is included. Use its displayed total duration to plan your time.
## Link and start
Select a routine in mission details, open Record mission, then tap Measure and record. The routine selector also appears in the measurement screen even when none is selected. Review permission prompts, including location for routes.
## Editing and temporarily saved sessions
Pause measurement before changing, removing or editing a routine. Select it in the routine area; the more menu retains Edit current routine, Measurement settings, Photo settings and Sound settings. Earlier actual activity remains saved and a replacement begins at its first activity only after Resume. Sound settings offer BPM groups with short exercise suggestions.
## Review and save
Save the actual result and check the history. The mission criteria determine success, not the routine's planned time. You can manually enter an exercise completed without a routine when the mission has suitable input fields.

## Measurement and routine tabs

Below the elapsed time, the measurement screen has Measurement and Routine tabs. Measurement opens first and contains the repetition counter. Without a routine, the timer shows elapsed time without a planned total. Once a routine is fully completed, Continue execution is disabled on the finish sheet. Early finishes and measurement without a routine can still continue.

[Routines](/routines/) · [History and feed](/records/)

/guides/video-feed/.title: Create a video post
/guides/video-feed/.description: Create a video post · MP4 · ZIP
/guides/video-feed/.markdown:
# Your records over a moving scene
Add your results to a clip of your run or workout. Video tools require a supported recent app version; menus may differ in older installations.
## Import a video
In the feed composer, open + and select an album video, up to 512MB per file. The app copies it into private device storage without uploading it to a company server. You can use photos or videos without adding records; record cards are never inserted automatically.
## Frame and trim
Choose Fit video to keep the whole scene or Fill video to cover the frame. Fill also offers zoom and horizontal and vertical positioning. Drag the two segment handles to choose the start and end; the original stays unchanged.
Place selected records, text and stickers on the video and adjust dimming. Measurement labels and values stay inline. Format all text or individual items, and adjust labels, values and units separately if desired.
## Watch in the feed
The visible video starts muted, plays automatically and loops the selected segment. Tap it to pause or resume in place. Videos with audio show a speaker button for preview sound. Leaving the screen or putting the app in the background stops playback.
Tapping a photo opens its viewer. Pinch to zoom from 1× to 5× and pan the enlarged photo.
## Sound and sharing
Mute shared video controls audio in the exported MP4. The feed speaker button changes preview sound only and does not change export settings.
Sharing creates an MP4 on the device with your selected segment and visible overlays. Photos and videos can be shared together; the receiving app determines supported file formats. Saving a post does not publish it to other people.
## Backups contain the whole original
A ZIP backup includes editing settings and the complete original video, including parts trimmed out of the post. Consider this before sending a backup. Editing does not modify or delete the album original, and imported videos are not automatically duplicated in the gallery.
[Records and feed](/records/) · [Get started](/download/)
